result.title: Beyond Gain: Measuring Skill Internalization for Agent Skill Retirement
result.summary: LLM agents retrieve skills from public hubs that hold up to about 100,000 entries and serve many models. As models improve, a hub must find the skills a given model has internalized, meaning it can do without them, and retire them for that model, yet internalization has not been measured with known reliability. Published rules that compare runs with and without a skill retire on the gain alone. The gain is near zero both for an internalized skill and when neither the model nor the skill delivers the capability, a state we call uncovered. We instead withhold the skill, score the model on a task synthesized from it, and trust a high unaided score only when another model gains from the skill, since nearly half of high scores come from tasks no model benefits from. Under four models, a published gain rule applied with one task per skill removes over half of the uncovered skills. On SkillsBench, 28 of its 31 retirements rest on probes no run passed in full, while retiring on the unaided score costs no detectable reward. Unaided verdicts reproduce across tasks more often than the gain rule's (Cohen's kappa 0.42 against 0.23) but differ across models, so a hub must read them per model. We release 1,251 skills with tasks and item scores under four models.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究如何判定某模型已「内化」某技能、从而可在公共技能库中为其退役该技能；作者不沿用仅比较有无技能增益的规则，而是撤除技能后用由其合成的任务测模型的无辅助得分，并要求其他模型确实从该技能获益作为对照，另发布 1,251 条技能及四模型下的任务与分项评分。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「撤除某一外部组件＋用他人是否获益来排除无信息试探」的能力归因协议，可能可供核查 LVR 中 latent 状态或视觉旁路是否真被答案使用，并区分「模型本已会用而无增益」与「模型与组件都不提供该能力」两种零增益情形。
